verdict: Marsh McLennan grew revenue 8% to $6.9B and profit 8% to $808M — steady, broad-based growth across insurance broking and consulting, with adjusted EPS up 10%.

segments.name: Risk & Insurance Services
segments.note: Marsh (the world's largest insurance broker) and Guy Carpenter (reinsurance broking) — placing insurance for companies and earning commissions and fees, plus fiduciary interest income on premiums held in trust.

segments.name: Consulting
segments.note: Mercer (people, retirement and investments advice) and Oliver Wyman (management consulting, +14%).

segments.name: Corporate eliminations
segments.note: Intercompany eliminations and corporate items — a small negative that brings the segments to total revenue.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Offices, technology, travel and amortization of intangibles from acquisitions — the line that separates GAAP operating income ($1.2B) from adjusted ($1.5B).

otherDetail: Interest expense of $248M, partly offset by $48M of pension benefit credits, $10M of interest income and $8M of investment income.

takeaways.title: Both halves grew
takeaways.text: Risk & Insurance Services revenue rose 7% to $4.2B and Consulting 9% to $2.7B — no single deal or region carried the quarter; underlying growth was 5%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS outran GAAP again
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS rose 10% to $2.03, ahead of GAAP's $1.69. The gap is mostly amortization of intangibles from Marsh's many acquisitions, which management excludes.

takeaways.title: Oliver Wyman stood out
takeaways.text: Management consulting revenue jumped 14%, the fastest-growing piece of the portfolio, while the big broking business compounded steadily.

footerNote: Marsh McLennan does not report a cost-of-revenue line. For a people business, its $4,078M of compensation and benefits — the brokers and consultants clients actually pay for — is treated here as the direct cost of revenue, and its other operating expenses as running costs. The company files its reports as Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc.
